about_me.title: About me
about_me.paragraph:
I'm a student and developer passionate about creating modern web applications. I work across the whole stack, building applications with React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, PostgreSQL and newly ASP.NET. My projects focus on smooth user experiences, efficient data handling, and solid technical foundations.

I like exploring and learning new technologies and improving how things are built, whether it’s refining architecture, optimizing performance, or experimenting with better development workflows.

Outside of web development, I also explore game development in C++ and Unity.

tda26.title: Think Different Academy
tda26.brief: Think Different Academy is a web platform for engaging education created for the Tour de App 2026 competition. It allows lecturers to create interactive modules with materials and quizzes that students complete in real time.
tda26.description: Think Different Academy is a web platform for engaging education created as part of the Tour de App 2026 competition. It enables lecturers to prepare interactive modules with materials and quizzes that can be gradually revealed during lessons, while students complete the content in real time. The system also includes user management (branches, lecturers, students), result statistics, and gamification elements such as XP, virtual currency, and activity-based rewards. We placed 1st in the competition round and 3rd in the final, where the goal was to improve the application within 9 hours in terms of scalability, monetization, and user experience.

sections.title: Our Goal
sections.content:
To create a system where:
- The lecturer can prepare learning modules (materials + quizzes)  
- Content is gradually revealed during live lessons  
- Students can interactively respond and complete tasks

sections.title: Features
sections.content:
- Creation of modules with materials and quizzes  
- Gradual unlocking of content during lessons  
- Students complete quizzes in real time  
- Overview of student results and statistics  
- Lecturer-based student evaluation

sections.title: Architecture
sections.content:
- Structure: branches, lecturers, students
- Lecturers can invite students into the system  
- Students create accounts and access content 
- Frontend: NuxtJS, Backend: .NET 9, Database: MySQL and Redis

sections.title: Gamification
sections.content:
- XP system based on activity  
- Virtual currency (duck coins)  
- Daily tasks  
- Cosmetic rewards for activity

sections.title: Development and Scalability
sections.content:
During the final, within 9 hours, it was required to:
- Adjust the application for better scalability  
- Prepare a monetization model  
- Increase user engagement and enjoyment

sections.title: Added Value
sections.content:
- Combination of education and gamification  
- Increased student engagement  
- Simple content management for lecturers

monitoring-dashboard.title: Monitoring Dashboard
monitoring-dashboard.brief: A self-hosted uptime and incident monitoring tool built for clarity and reliability. It tracks service availability, logs incidents, handles maintenance windows, and generates daily uptime stats.
monitoring-dashboard.description: A self-hosted uptime and incident monitoring tool built for clarity and reliability. It tracks service availability, logs incidents, handles maintenance windows, and generates daily uptime stats, all powered by .NET 9, Blazor, and PostgreSQL. Background workers do the heavy lifting while a clean Tailwind-styled UI keeps everything easy to read.

slenderman.title: Slenderman
slenderman.brief: A short horror game clone built in Unreal Engine 5. Original game: Slender: The Eight Pages by Parsec Productions. It features page collection, basic enemy AI, and a full win/lose loop. Focused on learning C++, AI behavior and completing a playable game.
slenderman.description: A short horror game clone built in Unreal Engine 5. Original game: Slender: The Eight Pages by Parsec Productions. It features page collection, basic enemy AI, and a full win/lose loop. Focused on learning C++, AI behavior and completing a playable game.

intro.p1: A small horror game project inspired by Slender: The Eight Pages, built in Unreal Engine 5.
intro.p2: This project was for me to learn and finish developing a playable game in UE5. Not all planned features were implemented as I focused on finishing a playable version.

gameplay.title: 🕹️ Gameplay
items: Jump scares, ambient SFX, win/lose states

features.title: 🎮 Features Implemented
items: Basic AI: Slenderman moves and teleports around the player
Slenderman model and simple jumpscare system

planned.title: 🚧 Missing or Planned Features
planned.note: These may be added in a future polish update.

learned.title: 💡 What I Learned
items: Building a full gameplay loop from start to finish
Managing project scope and avoiding perfectionism
Using C++ to handle AI and interaction logic
Setting up pause/lose/win widgets in UE5
